meta.titre: Operating System Types: batch, real-time, time-sharing and network systems

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: At a bank branch in Douala, a program may process the day's transactions overnight while nobody sits at a keyboard. In a school computer room, thirty students may use one central computer at the same moment. Inside a car, the braking computer must react within a strict time limit. All these machines run operating systems, but not the same kind of operating system. Examiners ask you to name the types, to describe them with real-life examples, to say which features set one type apart from another and to place the early types in order. This course gives you the comparison that those questions need.

items: An operating system is the software that manages the hardware (processor, memory, storage, input and output devices) and provides services to programs and users.
A process is a program in execution, and the CPU is much faster than input and output devices, so it often has to wait for them.
A network is a group of computers connected so that they can share data and resources.

sections.titre: Types of operating system: purpose, features and examples
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Development in outline
Early computers were run by an operator who loaded one job at a time. In broad terms, the order of development was **batch systems**, then **multiprogramming**, then **time-sharing**, followed by personal computer, network and distributed systems; real-time systems grew up for control tasks.

### Main types
| Type | Main idea | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| Batch | similar jobs are collected and run as a group with no user interaction while they run | payroll, monthly bills |
| Multiprogramming | several programs are kept in memory; when one waits for input or output the CPU runs another, so the CPU is rarely idle | any system that wants high CPU utilisation |
| Time-sharing (multitasking) | CPU time is cut into short slices given in turn to the users or programs, so each gets a quick reply | multi-user servers, desktop and mobile systems |
| Real-time | the response must come within a fixed deadline | aircraft control, anti-lock brakes, a heart pacemaker |
| Network | runs on a server and provides shared files, printers, user accounts and security to the client computers of a network | a school or office network |
| Distributed | many networked computers behave as one system and the user does not know which computer does the work | large clusters of cooperating computers |
| Embedded | built into a device with a dedicated task and limited resources | a washing machine, a router |

A **hard** real-time system must never miss a deadline because a late result is a failure; a **soft** real-time system tolerates occasional lateness, as in video streaming. Real time means guaranteed response time, not simply speed.

A **single-user** system serves one person at a time; a **multi-user** system lets several users with separate accounts work on the same computer at the same time.

variantes.nom: Batch processing compared with real-time processing
variantes.quand_utiliser: Use for a question that asks you to describe both with real-life scenarios.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Criterion | Batch | Real time |
|---|---|---|
| Data | collected first, processed later in one run | processed as it arrives |
| User interaction | none while the job runs | inputs from sensors or users are answered at once |
| Response time | not urgent; hours may pass | limited by a strict deadline |
| Example | producing all the pay slips of a company at the end of the month | the control computer of an aircraft or of anti-lock brakes |
| If it is late | results are only delayed | hard real time: the system fails; soft real time: quality falls |

For each type, give the definition, one real scenario and the reason why it matches the definition.

variantes.nom: Network operating system compared with distributed operating system
variantes.quand_utiliser: Use to separate the two terms, which are often confused.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
| Feature | Network OS | Distributed OS |
|---|---|---|
| Computers | each has its own operating system and works independently | act together as one system |
| User's view | knows which server, printer or computer holds a resource | does not know where a resource or a task is: transparency |
| Main purpose | share files, printers, accounts and security | share the load and run one task on several computers |
| Typical feature | central user management, backup and security on a server | tasks are placed on any suitable computer by the system |

A statement such as "the user does not know where the resources are" describes a distributed system, not a network operating system.

variantes.quand_utiliser: Use when these three similar terms must be defined or distinguished.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
- **Multiprogramming**: several programs are in memory together and the CPU moves to another one when the running program waits for input or output. The aim is to keep the CPU busy.
- **Multitasking** (time-sharing): the CPU also moves on when a short time slice ends, so every program gets regular turns and the user sees fast replies.
- **Multiprocessing**: the computer has more than one processor, so several processes really run at the same instant.

sections.enonce_markdown:
Name the most suitable type of operating system for each situation and give one reason.

(a) A water company's computer prepares the bills of all its customers in one overnight run; the data was typed in during the day and no operator is needed.
(b) The computer of an anti-lock braking system reads the wheel sensors and must always react within a fixed, very short time.
(c) Thirty students in a computer room in Buea log in at the same time to one central computer, and each gets replies quickly.
(d) A school office has one server that stores shared documents and user accounts; each teacher works on a personal computer with its own operating system.

etapes.action: Identify the key feature in each scenario before naming a type.
etapes.justification: The command word is "name and give a reason", so each answer needs the type and the matching feature.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Key features: (a) no interaction and a group of jobs; (b) a strict deadline; (c) many users sharing one computer; (d) a server serving clients.

etapes.justification: Jobs are collected, run as a group and need no user interaction while running.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) **Batch processing.** The delay of a few hours matters little.

etapes.justification: A late result would be a failure, so the system must guarantee the response time.
The CPU is shared in short slices among several users who interact with the computer.
A server provides shared files and accounts to client computers that keep their own operating systems.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (d) **Network operating system**; it is not distributed, because the teachers know that they use the server.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a) batch; (b) hard real-time; (c) time-sharing multi-user; (d) network operating system.** A good answer always links the type to the feature seen in the scenario, not only to a name.

items.erreur_markdown: A real-time system is simply a very fast system.
items.pourquoi_faux: Real time means that the response time is guaranteed to meet a deadline. A fast system can still miss a deadline, and a slow process with a long deadline can be real time.
items.correction_markdown: Define real time by the deadline, and give hard and soft examples.

items.erreur_markdown: Time-sharing and batch processing are the same because both run many jobs.
items.pourquoi_faux: In batch processing jobs run as a group with no interaction; in time-sharing users interact with the computer and the CPU is shared in short time slices.
items.correction_markdown: Contrast the two by interaction and by the way the CPU is shared.

items.erreur_markdown: In a batch system the user can type new data while the job is running.
items.pourquoi_faux: All the input is prepared before the job starts; the user does not interact with the job while it runs.
items.correction_markdown: Say that input is collected beforehand and output is returned after the run.

items.erreur_markdown: In a network operating system the users do not know where the resources are.
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes a distributed system. In a network operating system users know the server, printer or shared folder that they use.
items.correction_markdown: Keep transparency for the distributed operating system.

items.erreur_markdown: A network operating system is the operating system of any computer that is connected to a network.
items.pourquoi_faux: A network operating system is software that manages a server and its services (shared files, printers, accounts, security) for the client computers.
items.correction_markdown: Define it by the services that it gives to the clients.

items.enonce_markdown:
Say whether each system is best described as batch, real-time or time-sharing, and give one reason.

(a) A central computer prints the monthly statements of all the accounts of a savings cooperative in one run.
(b) The computer of an automatic gate must open the barrier at once when a sensor detects the approaching vehicle.
(c) Several staff members at a hospital reception use one central computer from their terminals at the same time.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Batch**: a group of similar jobs run without interaction and the result is not urgent. (b) **Real-time**: a response is needed within a fixed short time after the sensor input. (c) **Time-sharing**: the CPU is shared in short slices among interactive users.

items.enonce_markdown:
A time-sharing computer serves 25 users. Each user gets a time slice of 40 ms in turn, and each change from one user to the next costs 2 ms of switching. Assume that every user always wants the CPU.

(a) How long is one complete round of the 25 users?
(b) What fraction of each turn is used for useful work, as a percentage to one decimal place?
(c) Say what the user notices if the number of users increases and the slice stays the same.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) One turn = 40 + 2 = 42 ms, so one round = 25 x 42 = 1050 ms = 1.05 s. A user waits about 1.05 s between two turns.

(b) Useful fraction = 40 / 42 = 0.952, that is **95.2 %**.

(c) The round gets longer in proportion to the number of users, so each user waits longer between turns and the system seems slower.

**Round: 1050 ms; useful work: 95.2 %.**

items.enonce_markdown:
In a simple model of multiprogramming, each program spends 70 % of its time waiting for input and output, the programs wait independently, and the CPU is idle only when all the programs in memory are waiting. With n programs in memory, the CPU utilisation is 1 - 0.7^n.

(a) Calculate the utilisation for n = 1, 2, 3 and 4.
(b) Find the smallest n for which utilisation is at least 90 %.
(c) Explain what this shows about the reason for multiprogramming.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) n = 1: 1 - 0.7 = 0.300, so **30.0 %**. n = 2: 1 - 0.49 = 0.51, so **51.0 %**. n = 3: 1 - 0.343 = 0.657, so **65.7 %**. n = 4: 1 - 0.2401 = 0.7599, so **76.0 %**.

(b) For n = 6: 1 - 0.117649 = 88.2 %, which is below 90 %. For n = 7: 1 - 0.0823543 = 91.8 %. **The smallest n is 7.**

(c) With one program the CPU is idle 70 % of the time while that program waits for input and output. Keeping several programs in memory lets the CPU run another program during each wait, so utilisation rises. The model is a simplification (the programs do not really wait independently), but it explains why multiprogramming was introduced after batch systems that ran one job at a time.

items_markdown: In outline, operating systems developed from batch systems to multiprogramming and then time-sharing, followed by personal computer, network and distributed systems.
Batch processing runs a group of jobs with no interaction (payroll, bills); real-time processing guarantees a response within a deadline (hard: aircraft control, anti-lock brakes; soft: streaming).
Multiprogramming keeps several programs in memory to keep the CPU busy; time-sharing adds short time slices for interactive users; multiprocessing means several processors.
A network operating system runs on a server and shares files, printers, accounts and security with clients that keep their own operating systems; users know where the resources are.
A distributed operating system makes several computers behave as one system, and the user does not see which computer does the work.
In an answer, give the definition, a real-life scenario and the feature that links the two.
